haemoglobin: An iron-rich protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body.
hemoglobin: An iron-rich protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body.
mcv: Measures the average size of your red blood cells to help classify blood characteristics.
mch: Measures the average amount of hemoglobin inside a single red blood cell.
mchc: Measures the concentration of hemoglobin within a given volume of packed red blood cells.
rbc: The count of red cells that transport vital oxygen throughout your body tissues.
wbc: The primary white cells of your immune system that defend your body against infections.
total leukocyte count: The total number of infection-fighting white blood cells circulating in your bloodstream.
platelet count: Cell fragments that help your blood clot normally to prevent excessive bleeding.
tsh: A hormone from your pituitary gland that signals your thyroid gland how much thyroid hormone to produce.
free t3: The active, unattached form of triiodothyronine hormone regulating your body's energy and metabolism.
free t4: The primary circulating thyroid hormone available for tissues to convert into active metabolic hormone.
total cholesterol: The total amount of all circulating cholesterol types (fats) measured in your blood stream.
triglycerides: A type of fat in your blood that stores unused calories and provides cellular energy between meals.
hdl: Often termed 'protective' cholesterol because it helps carry excess cholesterol back to your liver.
hdl cholesterol: Often termed 'protective' cholesterol because it helps carry excess cholesterol back to your liver.
ldl: Cholesterol particles that carry lipids through the bloodstream to supply cells with essential structural fats.
ldl cholesterol: Cholesterol particles that carry lipids through the bloodstream to supply cells with essential structural fats.
vldl: Particles produced by your liver to transport triglycerides to tissues across your body.
fasting blood glucose: Measures your circulating blood sugar level after fasting overnight for at least 8 to 10 hours.
glucose: The main type of sugar in your blood that acts as your body's primary immediate energy fuel.
random blood sugar: Measures your current blood sugar level regardless of when you last had food or drink.
hba1c: Reflects your average circulating blood sugar level over the preceding 2 to 3 months.
creatinine: A natural muscle waste product filtered out by healthy kidneys into the urine.
serum creatinine: A natural muscle waste product filtered out by healthy kidneys into the urine.
blood urea nitrogen: Measures the amount of nitrogen in your blood that comes from protein breakdown and waste processing.
bun: Measures the amount of nitrogen in your blood that comes from protein breakdown and waste processing.
uric acid: A byproduct created when the body breaks down natural chemicals called purines found in foods and cells.
egfr: An estimated calculation of how effectively and rapidly your kidneys are filtering blood fluids.
sgot: An enzyme found mainly in liver and heart cells; released into the blood when cells experience stress.
ast: An enzyme found mainly in liver and heart cells; released into the blood when cells experience stress.
sgpt: An enzyme found concentrated in liver cells; helps clinicians observe liver cell cellular integrity.
alt: An enzyme found concentrated in liver cells; helps clinicians observe liver cell cellular integrity.
bilirubin total: A yellow pigment formed during the normal natural breakdown of aged red blood cells.
alkaline phosphatase: An enzyme present throughout body tissues, especially concentrated in the liver and bone structures.
serum albumin: The most abundant blood protein produced by your liver that keeps fluid from leaking out of vessels.
total protein: Measures the combined amount of albumin and globulin proteins circulating in your bloodstream.
serum sodium: An essential electrolyte that controls fluid balance, blood pressure, and normal nerve/muscle signaling.
serum potassium: A vital electrolyte crucial for proper heart rhythm, cellular fluid regulation, and muscle contractions.
vitamin d: A fat-soluble nutrient essential for bone strength, calcium absorption, and healthy immune function.
vitamin b12: An essential vitamin needed for nerve tissue health, brain function, and red blood cell production.
serum ferritin: Measures the amount of stored iron currently held in reserve inside your body's cells.
crp: A protein synthesized by the liver that rises in response to general bodily immune activation or inflammation.
esr: Measures the rate at which red blood cells settle at the bottom of a test tube over one hour.
